name: Tricia Griffith

career.title: Claims representative, then managerial roles in the Claims division

background_rationale: Spent her entire career at Progressive, starting as a claims representative and rising through claims, human resources, customer operations and personal lines operating roles before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Under Griffith, Progressive pushed to bundle auto and home policies for customers it calls 'Robinsons', growing that group from about 400,000 to 1 million households in just over two years.
Discussing Progressive's Snapshot telematics data, Griffith said understanding which risks will have more losses is 'really the name of the game' in insurance.
Progressive reported 2025 companywide policies in force growth of 10%, net premiums written growth of 12%, a combined ratio of 87.4 and net income of $11.3 billion.

personal_story.hook: The daughter of a waitress and a door-to-door insurance salesman, Tricia Griffith joined Progressive as a claims rep and became CEO.
personal_story.summary: Griffith grew up in Illinois; her mother was a waitress and her father sold insurance door to door, and she has said those were the two jobs she did not want. After graduating from Illinois State University and a short stint in retail, she answered a classified ad and in 1988 joined Progressive as a claims representative in Indianapolis, at a salary of $19,200, expecting it to be temporary. About nine months in, she says, she fell in love with the company's values and the people she worked with. She rose through claims, became chief human resources officer in 2002 despite her own doubts that she could do it, and later ran claims, customer operations and personal lines before becoming the company's first female CEO in July 2016.
